facts.text: A common-cause failure is one event that disables two or more parts intended to back each other up; redundancy counts only when the channels are truly independent.
facts.quote: A common-cause failure is one event that knocks out two or more parts that were supposed to back each other up, so redundancy only counts when the channels are truly independent.

facts.text: A redundant design using two sensors, two processors or two brake circuits earns safety credit only when a single cause cannot fail both channels.
facts.quote: A redundant design (two sensors, two processors, two brake circuits) earns credit only when a single cause cannot fail both channels.

facts.text: Common causes of channel failure include a shared power supply, the same software bug, the same environmental stress such as dust on both lenses, the same wrong design assumption or the same calibration error.
facts.quote: Common causes include a shared power supply, the same software bug in both channels, the same environmental stress (dust on both lenses), the same wrong design assumption or the same calibration error.

facts.text: ISO 13849 uses a checklist to score common-cause failure defenses, including separation, diverse technologies and environmental protection.
facts.quote: ISO 13849 scores the defenses (separation, diverse technologies, environmental protection) with a checklist.

facts.text: Diversity is the strongest common-cause failure defense identified in the passage: radar and camera channels use different physics and fail in different conditions.
facts.quote: Diversity is the strongest: a radar and a camera use different physics and fail in different conditions.

facts.text: The sensor-fusion safety argument must include common-cause degradation and disagreement between sensing technologies because one storm can degrade several sensors.
facts.quote: For sensor fusion, the safety argument must include common-cause degradation and disagreement between sensing technologies, since one storm can degrade several sensors [Chapter 1].

facts.text: If the virtual sensor, collision logic and test oracle—the rule deciding pass or fail—embed the same simplifying assumption, a large virtual test campaign can produce very consistent but very misleading results.
facts.quote: if the virtual sensor, the collision logic and the test oracle (the rule deciding pass or fail) embed the same simplifying assumption, a large virtual campaign produces very consistent and very misleading results

facts.text: If the product and test environment share the same map, target model or physics simplification, a virtual test reproduces the same error twice.
facts.quote: if product and test environment share the same map, target model or physics simplification, a virtual test reproduces the same error twice.

facts.text: Independent real-world referents are the defense against shared-assumption errors in virtual testing.
facts.quote: Independent real-world referents are the defense [Chapters 12, 13].

facts.text: The aviation rule that a model cannot be validated by comparison with another validated model reflects the principle of independence against common-cause errors.
facts.quote: The aviation rule that a model cannot be validated by comparison with another validated model is the same principle [Chapter 10].

facts.text: A deterministic radar channel can bound what a machine-learning channel must prove, but only if the two channels fail differently.
facts.quote: A deterministic radar channel can bound what a machine-learning channel must prove, but only if the two fail differently [Chapter 1]

facts.text: Validation evidence for a simulator must come from a source that does not share the simulator's assumptions.
facts.quote: validation evidence for the simulator must come from a source that does not share its assumptions.
